group: Ball Lost or Out of Bounds
imagePrompt: Create a modern, semi-realistic illustration (about 75% realistic, 25% stylised) of a golf teeing area on a long hole. Show a player preparing to play a provisional ball from the tee with their club, while another player watches. In the distance, show the original ball flying towards a line of trees and white stakes marking out of bounds along the right edge of the fairway. The teeing area should have two balls visible: one in flight and one teed up. Do not include any text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer at the tee preparing to play a provisional ball with a club, while another player watches. In the background, the original ball is flying towards trees and white out of bounds stakes along the fairway.

sceneSpec.setting: The teeing area of a long hole, with a fairway bordered by trees and white stakes indicating an out of bounds line.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer just finishing their tee shot, another player nearby observing.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: The original ball is seen flying towards trees near the out of bounds line but still in flight; a second ball is set up on a tee, ready for a provisional shot.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The moment after the original tee shot, before playing a provisional ball.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Highlighting the option to play a provisional ball when unsure if the first is out of bounds.
mustShow: Tee area with two balls (one played, one teed up for provisional)
White stakes lining the edge of the fairway
Player preparing to play a provisional shot

questions.title: What to Do If You Think Your Ball Might Be Out
questions.question: You think your ball might be out of bounds, but you are not sure. What should you do before you go look for it?

choices.text: Walk up to where you think your ball is and then decide what to do.
Hit another ball now, just in case, and call it a provisional ball.
Say straight away that your first ball is lost.

questions.explanation: If you think your ball might be out of bounds, you can hit a provisional ball before walking to look for your first one. This saves time, in case your first ball cannot be found or is out of bounds.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A ball you play just in case your first ball is lost or out of bounds.
A place outside the golf course where you are not allowed to play from.

questions.teachingTip: Act out a situation where a ball might be out of bounds to show when to play a provisional ball.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think they must always look for their ball first.
They might think they cannot play a provisional ball unless an adult tells them.

questions.title: When to Play a Provisional Ball
questions.question: You think your ball may be out of bounds but are not certain. What should you do?

choices.text: Wait until you reach the area and decide.
Immediately declare the original ball lost.

questions.explanation: To save time, a player may play a provisional ball under Rule 18.3 if they think their ball may be lost outside a penalty area or out of bounds. This allows the player to avoid a long walk back if the original ball is not found or is out of bounds.
